chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) dyed (his beard), and he did not prevent Ali (peace be upon him) except for the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'You will be dyeing this (beard) from this (head wound)', and Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) had dyed.
ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad and the Imams dye their beards?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of beard dyeing by highlighting the consistent practice of the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically Ali, Al-Husayn, and Abu Ja'far. It resolves a potential ambiguity regarding Ali by explaining that his temporary restraint was due to a specific context of a head wound ('this from this'), rather than a general prohibition, thereby establishing a strong precedent for the Imams' personal use of henna or similar dyes.
